title: Localized content should follow target-language conventions, not source patterns
context: Hebrew changelog corpus (71 titles) is deliberately impersonal; v1.10.6 headline uniquely used second-person possessive שלכם, violating the established pattern. Published headlines are permanent, so correctness must be verified with native speakers before release.
decision: Remove possessive from Hebrew headline to match corpus convention. Allowed each locale (Hebrew, Russian, Spanish, Arabic) to follow its own linguistic rules rather than force-match English's use of possessives.
consequences: Hebrew localization now internally consistent across all 71 changelog titles
Established precedent: locale-specific linguistic choices override source-language literal translation
Requires native speaker review before publishing user-facing content
All four locales verified as self-consistent in their own grammatical conventions
alternatives_rejected: Keep possessive to match English literally
Standardize grammatical patterns across all locales regardless of target-language norms

rejected_tripwires.alternative: Keep possessive to match English literally
